ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT framework), as amended, regulated by Executive Decree No. 165 de 26 de julio de 2016; Executive Decree No. 452 de 14 de julio de 2020 creating and regulating the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF); Law No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 on Private Interest Foundations; applicable resolutions and regulations issued by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) of Panama.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry or Chamber of Commerce in the founder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or Consular Legalization by a Panamanian Consul if the origin country is not an Apostille signatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Founder Board Resolution Approving the Creation of the Panama Private Interest Foundation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate Secretary and Board of Directors of the Founder Entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the founder's jurisdiction and the founder's account-holding bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for the notary certification; original bank letter accepted under AML file if notarized by the bank officer

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-engagement and ongoing screening of all founders, foundation council members, protectors, beneficiaries, and counterparties against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Sanctions, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, the UAF's domestic national list, and Interpol or World Bank debarment sources. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth documentation, senior compliance officer approval, and immediate UAF consultation for any adverse screening hit. The IVD sector is classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced and therefore requires transaction-level screening for all Swift_LC and TT_Wire payment rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Servicios en Línea del Registro Público de Panamá — Name Search and Reservation Module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official language of registry documents is Spanish. Foundation names must be expressed in Roman/Latin script; a foreign-language name is permitted but must be accompanied by an official Spanish translation in the foundation charter. The corporate name must suitably distinguish the entity from all existing registered names and must comply with the public-order naming provisions of the Registro Público.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Público rejects a name application, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request (recurso de reconsideración) with the Dirección General del Registro Público within 5 business days of the refusal notice, accompanied by evidence that the proposed name remains compliant and distinguishable. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file a jerarchic appeal or an administrative contentious action (demanda contencioso-administrativa) before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso Administrativo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia within 2 months of the final administrative decision. A fresh name reservation must be filed if the original reservation lapses or is exhausted during the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For the Private Interest Foundation used as an IVD holding vehicle, a virtual or serviced office is acceptable only as a registered-office address and for receipt of notices. It is not accepted as evidence of commercial substance for purposes of obtaining a Panamanian sanitary license, MINSA import authorization, or an operating facility for IVD manufacturing. If the foundation intends to engage in substantive IVD distribution or manufacturing, a physical leased or owned facility is required by prevailing regulatory practice and banking AML expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 10–15% per year for a passive PIF with no local operations; increases to 55–70% per year once the PIF or its operating subsidiary applies for a sanitary license, registers with the Panamanian Ministry of Health, or imports IVD analyzers under a Panamanian tax ID.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Law 25 of June 12, 1995) on Private Interest Foundations (PIFs), as amended by Law 18 of 2011 and Law 3 of 2016 (AML/CFT amendments); Articles 7, 18-26 (endowment, charter content, foundation council, and registry requirements).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama - Private Interest Foundations Section), Archivo de Fundaciones.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Constitutiva / Escritura de Fundación de Interés Privado (Foundation Charter executed as a notarized public deed and submitted for registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum foundation endowment of US$10,000 (B/.10,000) per Article 7 of Law 25 of 1995. The endowment may be composed of cash, securities, or other assets, must be fully subscribed by the founder in the Charter, and need not be placed in an escrow bank account; the Charter may provide for staged contribution of the endowment within a defined timeline.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDER AND THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME]: WHEREAS, the Foundation Charter was notarized on [date] and is being presented to the Public Registry under Law 25 of 1995. RESOLVED: the Charter, comprising the foundation purpose, the US$10,000 minimum endowment, and the registered office at [address], Panama, is ratified and adopted, and [Law Firm] is appointed Resident Agent. RESOLVED FURTHER: [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Guardian; each may execute agreements, open bank accounts, and bind the Foundation. RESOLVED FURTHER: the officers shall implement all steps required to obtain industrial, environmental, and health licenses for the IVD manufacturing facility.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation KYC and Foundation Charter Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian attorney (abogado idóneo) at a law firm registered with the Superintendencia de Mercado de Valores / AML compliance officer under Law 23 of 2015 and CRF regulations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Panamanian counsel to conduct client due diligence (beneficial owner identification, source of funds verification), verify proposed foundation name availability in the Public Registry, draft the Foundation Charter and private Reglamento (internal rules), and prepare the registered agent acceptance letter and powers of attorney.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of founder's passport or national ID
Bank reference and source of funds/wealth statement
Certificate of good standing and constitutional documents of corporate founder (if applicable)
Proposed foundation name and purpose statement
Structured beneficial ownership information (name, address, nationality of beneficiaries)
Letter of instructions for attorney engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected at pre-vetting, counsel files an alternate reserved name with the Registry and amends the draft Charter accordingly without additional Registry penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública (Notary Public) of Panama designated by the firm's principal notary office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder or authorized representative appears before the Notary Public to execute the Foundation Charter. The Notary verifies identity and legal capacity, witnesses signature, and records the deed in the notarial protocol; the Resident Agent executes the acceptance statement. The notarized deed is then ready for presentation to the Public Registry.
required_dossiers: Finalized Foundation Charter text
Foundation name reservation confirmation
Notarized identification documents of the founder and foundation council members
Resident Agent acceptance letter
Proof of legal capacity of any corporate founder (board resolution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary identifies irregularities in identification or the proposed charter language, the attorney corrects the instrument and re-executes execution within the same notarial session; apostilled foreign documents are re-submitted after translation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Public Registry - Private Interest Foundations Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Counsel submits the notarized Foundation Charter, the legal opinion, and the official registry filing application with proof of payment of government fees (via Banco Nacional de Panamá or the Registry's digital payment portal). The Registry indexes the Charter, issues an inscription number (asiento), and returns the registered certificate and file number.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Foundation Charter (sufficient copies)
Legal opinion letter from counsel (dictamen legal)
Official government fee payment receipt (US$650 base plus page charges)
Name reservation confirmation (foja)
Registry application form signed by the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a 'nota de prevención' (observation notice) for formal defects (e.g., missing recitals or irregular amendments), counsel files the corrective written brief and supporting instrument within the granted cure period (usually 10 business days); upon correction the registration proceeds without restarting the queue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Municipal Registration (RUC and Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administración Nacional de Ingresos (ANIP, formerly DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance; Municipality of Panama (and district where registered office is located).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Registry-issued foundation certificate, counsel applies for the foundation's RUC (taxpayer identification number) at ANIP, designating the tax domicile and filing a Declaration of Business Commencement under territorial scope; concurrently, the Municipality registration (Aviso de Operación) is filed for the administrative/representative office, with industrial activity codes to be confirmed at the manufacturing site licensing stage.
required_dossiers: Registry certificate of the Private Interest Foundation
Certified copy of the Foundation Charter
Officer and foundation council appointment documents
Identification and RUC/PAN of resident agent
Municipal Aviso de Operación form with lease agreement of registered office
Utilities bill or notarized lease as proof of address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ANIP or the Municipality queries the foundation's economic activity classification, counsel submits an explanatory brief plus the business plan describing the IVD manufacturing scope and territorial income treatment, and, if necessary, files an updated declaration with revised ISIC codes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Statutory Books and Registered Office Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Resident Agent (licensed law firm) and Secretariat of the Foundation under Law 25 of 1995.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foundation's statutory records are created: Minutes Book of the Foundation Council (Libro de Actas), Beneficial Owners Register (Libro de Registro de Beneficiarios), and Foundation Council resolutions file. The Resident Agent files the registered office acceptance, and the officers execute a notarized declaration of the registered address for use in banking and licensing filings.
required_dossiers: Registered certificate and foundation file number
Appointment of officers and Guardian (Protector)
Notarized registered office declaration
Foundation Council resolution approving the books
Establishment of record-keeping policy under Law 3 of 2016
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Resident Agent changes or the registered address is questioned by the Registry or the Comptroller of the Archive, the Foundation Council executes a change-of-registered-agent amendment, which is notarized and filed with the Public Registry within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) - Dirección de Industrias, Registro de Establecimientos Industriales, under Law 28 of 1995 and its implementing regulations; sanitation licensing concurrently by the Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) - Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas (DNFD).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación Industrial / Licencia de Funcionamiento Industrial (MICI) for the manufacturing facility, together with the Permiso Sanitario de Funcionamiento para Fabricantes de Dispositivos Médicos de Diagnóstico In Vitro and product Registro Sanitario de Dispositivo Médico (IVD) issued by MINSA-DNFD.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Departamento de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental (Department of Environmental Impact Assessment).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II (Moderate Impact) - requires submission of an Environmental Impact Study (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental, case-study type) for an IVD microfluidic cartridge and immunoassay analyzer manufacturing facility that will use chemical buffers, photoresists, and assay reagents, and generate moderate wastewater and biological waste streams.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater effluents must meet Panama's water-quality norms (Executive Decree No. 509 of 2000): pH 6.0-9.0, BOD5 <= 50 mg/L, COD <= 200 mg/L, TSS <= 100 mg/L, oils and greases <= 10 mg/L; air emissions must comply with DGNTI-COPANIT air-quality emission limits (VOCs, particulate matter); all hazardous chemical waste and biological assay waste must be autoclaved or chemically neutralized on-site and manifested to a MiAMBIENTE-authorized waste handler; no untreated discharge to surface waters or municipal sewers is permitted without a discharge permit from IDAAN/ARSA and MiAMBIENTE.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (Certificado del Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá) issued under Law 34 of 1997 after inspection of fire suppression systems, emergency exits, and hazardous material storage; structural load inspection certificate from the Municipal Engineering Department confirming building suitability for ISO Class 8 cleanroom and analyzer assembly equipment; occupational safety clearance from the Ministry of Labor and Labor Development (MITRADEL) under Law 7 of 1975, including workplace exposure assessments for isopropyl alcohol and formaldehyde-free reagents, chemical hygiene plan, and employee medical surveillance protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) - Panama; electronic portal SITIO (Sistema Integrado de Tributos, https://sitio.dgi.gob.pa); registration and taxpayer update portal RUES (Registro Único de Contribuyente)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity or Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must first file its constitutive documents (e.g., foundation charter or branch registration) with the Panamanian Public Registry through a licensed resident agent/attorney. Once the public registration is effective, the resident legal representative submits the RUC application (Solicitud de Registro Único de Contribuyente) via the DGI/RUES portal or at DGI offices, including the certificate of public registry, certified articles/bylaws, resident agent acceptance, proof of registered address in Panama, and identification of the legal representative. The DGI assigns the RUC, and the taxpayer activates SITIO digital credentials. Before commencing taxable business in Panama, an Aviso de Operación must be obtained from the corresponding municipality, and where applicable, e-invoicing certification must be obtained from DGI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch entity classification election. A Private Interest Foundation is treated as an entity-level taxpayer on Panama-source income only; foreign-source income is outside the Panamanian tax base. No election exists to disregard the foundation. Available statutory choices include voluntary ITBMS registration, special export zero-rating registration, and application of preferential regimes such as free zones, Panama Pacifico, SEM (headquarters), and Ciudad del Saber if qualifying.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary turnover threshold; any person or entity habitually carrying out taxable sales of goods or services in Panama, including through a permanent establishment or registered branch, must obtain RUC and register for ITBMS (PAB/USD).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing (Factura Electrónica de Panamá, FEL) for VAT-registered taxpayers. Invoices must be issued through DGI-certified software or DGI's free e-invoicing platform, generated in XML format, digitally signed, and transmitted to DGI for validation. DGI validation returns a tracking code (Código de Trazabilidad) and QR code for each invoice, enabling fiscal clearance and audit trail. Fiscal printer invoices are gradually being replaced; only DGI-validated electronic invoices are acceptable for input VAT credits and documentary substantiation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods (including microfluidic cartridges and immunoassay analyzers) and of services actually rendered outside Panama qualify for ITBMS zero-rating, provided the seller is registered for ITBMS, is recognized as an exporter, the transaction produces foreign currency proceeds, and the goods or services physically leave/are consumed outside Panama. The zero rate must be supported by documentary evidence of export within the tax period; otherwise domestic 7% ITBMS applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Panama Customs Export Declaration (DUSAR/Declaración Única de Exportación, validated through SICE)
Bill of Lading (original or certified copy) or airway bill evidencing dispatch from Panama
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank confirmation (SWIFT or TT) showing export proceeds received in Panama or in the exporter's Panamanian bank account from the foreign buyer
Commercial invoice in final form, clearly stating the good/service exported
Purchase order, sales contract, and any certificates/documents required by the destination country (e.g., certificate of origin, sanitary or IVD product licensing documents)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may audit export files up to the general five-year statute of limitations, verifying physical export, customs validation, and inward FX proceeds. If export documentation is missing, false, or inconsistent, DGI may claw back the zero-rating and assess the 7% ITBMS, plus monthly interest and surcharges. Fraudulent zero-rating claims may attract penalties of 100%-200% of the omitted tax, civil fines, cancellation of the exporter registration, and criminal liability for tax and customs fraud; provincial customs authorities may additionally impose penalties under Panama's customs framework.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No central bank exists in Panama. The banking and foreign-exchange regulator of the International Banking Center is the Superintendency of Banks of Panama (Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá, 'SBP'). The monetary system is governed by Decree-Law No. 8 of 1904 and the 1972 Monetary Agreement with the United States, under which the U.S. dollar is full legal tender; the Panamanian balboa exists only as a unit of account for fractional coinage and circulates at a 1:1 parity with USD. Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as the fiscal agent of the Republic but performs no central-bank functions, does not issue currency, and exercises no exchange-control authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized territory with no capital or current-account restrictions, no central-bank visa procedure, and no convertibility hurdles for inbound investment, profit remittance, or capital repayment. Foreign-source income of a Private Interest Foundation is excluded under Panama's territorial tax regime, so its remittance abroad is free of Panamanian tax. However, Panamanian-source commercial profits derived by the foundation from its IVD manufacturing and trading activities are subject to the 25% corporate income tax under the Fiscal Code, and any distribution charged to those Panamanian-source profits attracts the 5% dividend withholding tax before the funds may be released abroad. Proper DGI filings and board resolutions are therefore the only practical prerequisites to an unimpeded outward remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Panama imposes no surrender, repatriation, conversion, or retention requirement on export proceeds. There is no statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for medical-device export receipts; USD and other foreign currency may be held freely in SBP-licensed banks or offshore accounts. Exporters must still comply with the AML/CFT documentation duties set out in Law 23 of 2015 and Decree No. 52 of 2015, which require banks to evidence the commercial reality of unusual transaction flows.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Trade Finance and Working Capital Account
Operational Account / USD Demand Deposit Account with Trade Services
Capital Escrow / Fiscal Agent Account and Public-Sector Disbursement Interface
Operational Account and Commercial Letter-of-Credit Facility
Cross-Border USD Transactional Account / Private Banking Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Panama-domiciled private interest foundations are rarely accepted by offshore digital EMIs (Wise Business, Payoneer, Airwallex, Mercury) because those providers are not licensed by the SBP and their correspondent banks apply heightened scrutiny to Panamanian legal-person clients. Wise Business supports some LatAm entities, but onboarding for a Law 25 foundation usually requires full audited documentation, UBO declarations, and a live operating history; many EMIs ultimately reject the foundation account class or restrict inflow from third parties. Legally, no non-bank EMI may operate a licensed domestic payment system in Panama without SBP authorization, so any EMI balance should be used only as a supplementary operating wallet, with the SBP-regulated bank account remaining the primary clearing and treasury rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one natural-person settlor or director with account-signature authority, together with the ultimate beneficial owner information, must be presented to the compliance unit at onboarding. Most Tier-1 Panamanian banks require a face-to-face interview in Panama City for medium-risk legal entities such as a PIF engaged in commercial manufacturing; several private banks permit remote onboarding through video conference when the introducer is an established Panamanian registered-agent firm, all documents are notarized and apostilled, and the bank's compliance committee approves the waiver. Digital-only, zero-presence account opening is not generally available for this entity class.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: AML risk flag: Private Interest Foundation without commercial track record; perceived as an asset-holding haven vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the foundation charter (Fundación de Interés Privado) filed under Law 25 of 1995; registered-agent certificate issued by a licensed Panamanian law firm; current beneficial-owner register kept under Law 23 of 2015 and reported under the Beneficial Ownership Registry (Law 254 of 2021); initial endowment deed and source-of-funds statement; board resolution appointing the account signatories; reviewed or audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ISIC 3250 / IVD manufacturer exposure: medical-device export revenue and distributor commissions to Latin American markets
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ministry of Health of Panama (MINSA) sanitary registration or official import/export permit for IVD devices; CE certificate under IVDR 2017/746 or FDA 510(k)/EUA authorizations evidencing authentic manufacturing activity; ISO 13485 certificate; executed commercial agreements with third-party distributors; proforma invoices, purchase orders, and transport documents (bills of lading or airway bills) matching forecast wire flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border USD wires to tax-haven and closed-currency jurisdictions (e.g., China, UAE, Mexico)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master sales contracts, per-transaction commercial invoices, packing lists, freight-forwarder receipts, correspondent-bank reference letters, and a group AML manual; SWIFT MT103 records matching underlying transactions; independent sanctions and PEP screening reports for all counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear economic substance of the Panamanian legal vehicle and absence of 'manage and control' activity evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance file: board-meeting minutes, written policies, main bank-account activity, payroll or BPO agreements, office-leasing contracts in Panama, registered-agent confirmation letter, and any annual foundation tax returns filed with the DGI for Panamanian-source income.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial and follow-on capital contributions from shareholders or founders should be transmitted by SWIFT MT103 USD credit to the foundation's USD account at its SBP-licensed Panamanian bank. Panama applies no central-bank filing or exchange-control purpose code; however, the remitter must state a clear payment reason (e.g., 'Capital contribution to Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995') and the foundation's Public Registry Folio and RUC, since the receiving bank's Know-Your-Transaction screen requires an economic-purpose description. For contributions above USD 1 million, the compliance package must include the endowment deed, the remitting entity's board resolution, a source-of-funds statement, and a group ownership/UBO chart. The foundation must maintain its registered agent, registered office, and beneficial-ownership registry filing; obtaining a RUC at the DGI is required before engaging in Panamanian commercial activity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational supplier payments, distributor refunds, and service fees are cleared via SWIFT MT103 transfers containing the UETR (field 111) and the underlying invoice reference. Large-ticket procurement of microfluidic cartridges, analyzers, and clinical reagents is routed through commercial documentary letters of credit issued under UCP 600 by the Panamanian bank through its U.S. correspondent (SWIFT MT700/MT707). Domestic USD obligations are settled via the Panamanian automated clearing house and interbank same-day transfers operated by Banco Nacional de Panamá, while intra-group treasury concentration may use zero-balance sweep structures at the SBP-regulated bank; cash volumes should remain consistent with the stated medical-device trade flows to minimize enhanced-outlier monitoring.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, CHF/USD) executed with an SBP-licensed bank or its international branch
Cross-currency swaps (XCS) covering EUR or CNY trade exposure, governed by an ISDA Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or illiquid Asian/LatAm currencies (e.g., CNY, MXN, ARS) booked through an offshore licensed counterparty because the Panamanian market lacks those deliverable pairs
Plain-vanilla OTC currency options on deliverable pairs to cap depreciation risk on distributor invoicing currencies
Interest-rate swap or cross-currency basis swap combinations linked to the commercial LC and trade-loan facilities to neutralize floating-rate exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax for Private Interest Foundations (Tasa Anual de Fundación de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá / Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of each calendar year; applicable from the second year following registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment after 31 May incurs an administrative surcharge of USD 100.00; persistent non-payment beyond two consecutive years may result in the foundation being declared delinquent and subsequently struck off the Public Registry, with loss of legal standing and enforceability of foundation acts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May, aligned with the annual franchise tax cycle; any transfer or replacement of the founder, protector, council member, or beneficiary with effective ownership must be updated within 30 days of the transaction.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or materially incomplete confirmation subjects the foundation to administrative fines under Law 23 of 2015 and its implementing decrees, typically ranging from USD 250.00 to USD 5,000.00; continuing non-compliance may suspend the issuance of certificates of good standing and entrains enforcement proceedings with the Tax Authority.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit is imposed on a Private Interest Foundation under Panama's Law 25 of 1995. An independent audit becomes mandatory only when (i) the foundation charter or trust instrument expressly requires it, (ii) a court or other competent authority orders an audit in the interests of creditors, beneficiaries, or the public, or (iii) the foundation conducts commercial activities within Panama that generate gross annual revenue exceeding the DGI threshold for audited financial statements, generally applied at USD 3,000,000 or as adjusted from time to time by the tax administration.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by Panama; no separate local GAAP is available for Panamanian legal entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Panama's beneficial ownership regime requires every Private Interest Foundation to maintain current information on its founder, foundation council members, protector (if any), and beneficiaries who ultimately own or control the foundation directly or indirectly. Annual confirmation shall revalidate the accuracy of such information with the DGI RUB. Any transfer of an ownership interest, change of council member, or modification of beneficiary rights must be reported within 30 days of the change; the annual confirmation is triggered by the calendar year cycle and must be completed prior to 31 May.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Protector or Supervisory Guardian (where appointed)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 – USD 1,800 per annum depending on the resident agent's services, UBO administration, and document custody.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not compulsory; voluntary independent audit under IFRS is estimated at USD 3,500 – USD 7,500 per annum for a typical private foundation with moderate asset activity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% on net taxable income derived from Panamanian sources under Panama's territorial income tax system.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general manufacturing tax holiday or patent box. The territorial regime excludes non-Panamanian-source income, but Panamanian-source income is fully taxable at 25%. Tax losses may be carried forward for five years. A qualifying Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime may tax certain foreign-source services at 0%, but this does not apply to ordinary IVD manufacturing or local distribution. Deductions are restricted to costs directly attributable to generating Panamanian-source income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 1041 (Declaración Jurada Anual del Impuesto sobre la Renta – Personas Jurídicas), filed electronically through the DGI e-Tax 2.0 portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance income tax payments are required during the active tax year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after fiscal year-end. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the deadline is 31 March of the following year. No automatic extension is available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all gross receipts arising from Panamanian sources, including domestic IVD analyzer sales, microfluidic cartridge sales, service contracts, rental of diagnostic equipment, and royalty income attributable to use of IP in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PIF with no Panamanian-source commercial activity should enter zero and attach a territorial-source schedule explaining the absence of Panamanian nexus.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report only deductible expenses directly attributable to the production of Panamanian-source income, including cost of goods sold, depreciation of analyzers and molds, wages, rent, utilities, freight, and local administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may deduct only expenses supported by Panamanian books and records and economically connected to Panamanian-source income; offshore overhead must be allocated using arm's-length allocation principles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute gross Panamanian-source income less allowable deductions and any permitted prior-year tax loss carryforward, subject to transfer pricing and territorial-source adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Net taxable income should reflect only Panamanian-source activity; losses carried forward may only offset Panamanian-source profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Multiply net taxable income by 25% to determine the nominal corporate income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero if no Panamanian-source net taxable income is declared.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2(b) - Advance payments tax credits and withholdings
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit quarterly corporate income tax advance payments, third-party withholding taxes, and other creditable payments already made to the DGI during the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach payment receipts and any withholding certificates issued by Panamanian payers; non-residents cannot claim refunds for foreign withholding taxes against Panamanian ISR.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2(c) - Balance due or credit carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the net income tax payable after credits or the amount to be carried forward as a credit against future ISR liabilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Make full electronic payment by the statutory deadline even where a nil return is filed; late payment triggers surcharges and interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is sanctioned with fines in the range of B/.50 to B/.5,000; unpaid ISR is subject to a 10% surcharge and monthly interest at the applicable DGI rate (approximately 1.5% per month). Continuous non-filing may result in automatic DGI assessment, bank attachment, and registration in the Public Registry equivalent to a tax caution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Standard dividend withholding tax is 5% on distributions made out of net profits that have already been subject to Panamanian corporate income tax. Distributions from non-taxed or exempt profits are generally subject to a 10% withholding tax; distributions of invested capital are not taxable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Where a Panama double tax convention is in force, a non-resident shareholder must be the beneficial owner and submit a Panama Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) plus the foreign residence jurisdiction's TRC to the Panamanian withholding agent before payment. The payer must retain documentation showing treaty qualification. If excess withholding is applied, a refund claim may be filed with the DGI through the administrative reconsideration process. No treaty relief is automatic; the return and documentary file must evidence residence, beneficial ownership, and absence of treaty shopping.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-residents is generally not subject to Panamanian withholding where the underlying loan capital is not deployed in Panama; interest derived from Panamanian banking arrangements may attract resident withholding rates. Royalties for patents, trademarks, know-how, software, and similar IP used in Panama are Panamanian-source income and attract statutory withholding of 12.5% on gross amounts, subject to applicable treaty reduction to rates such as 5% or 10% where a DTA applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: PAB 1,000,000 (Panamanian balboas, pegged 1:1 with the US dollar). Taxpayers with aggregate related-party transactions at or above PAB 1,000,000 are required to prepare and maintain a Local File and, where applicable, a Master File. In addition, local operational rules and DGI guidance require arm's-length recordation and annual transfer pricing reporting for controlled transactions with non-resident affiliates in the IVD distribution and IP licensing chain.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), introduced by Law 70 of 2019 and extended by Cabinet Decree and DGI resolutions, apply to tax-resident juridical persons, including Private Interest Foundations that carry on relevant activities. Manufacturing, distribution, financing, leasing, headquarters, shipping, investment holding, and intellectual property exploitation are relevant activities. A PIF earning IVD-related royalties or engaging in distribution must demonstrate adequate physical presence, qualified employees, active management in Panama, and proportionate expenditures in Panama. An annual economic substance declaration is mandatory, and failure to satisfy substance requirements may result in fines, reassessment of foreign-source income as Panamanian-source, and possible strike-off of the entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Income Tax Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating Panamanian-source IVD revenue, mischaracterizing domestic sales as foreign-source income, inflating cost of goods sold with fictitious purchases, or using the PIF as a facade to conceal the true manufacturing owner in Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative reassessment of the evaded tax plus a surcharge of up to 100% of the unpaid tax and monthly interest; criminal prosecution under Panama's Fiscal Code and Penal Code may trigger imprisonment and criminal fines. DGI may attach bank accounts, freeze credits, and embargo movable and immovable assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and Foundation Council members who sign false declarations, participate in the fraud, or knowingly benefit from the evasion can be personally liable for civil restitution, subject to travel bans and disqualification, and exposed to imprisonment where criminal intent is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Panama PIF as the nominal owner of IVD patents, trademarks, or distribution rights without Panamanian employees, physical premises, active management, or operating expenses; failing to file the annual economic substance declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Panama ESR Law 70 of 2019 and accompanying regulations, non-compliance attracts monetary penalties, restrictions and potential nullification of the foundation's public registration, and reassessment of otherwise foreign-source profits as Panama-source taxable income at the 25% ISR rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The founder, council members, and officers who permit a shell structure without substance may be subject to personal fines and disqualification from holding Panamanian fiduciary offices; civil liability can attach for taxes, penalties, and interest if they knowingly caused the non-compliance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border related-party purchases of microfluidic cartridges, analyzer components, or IP licensing arrangements without an arm's-length pricing study, Local File/Master File, or correct transfer pricing informative return; back-to-back invoicing priced at non-arm's-length margins.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may disregard improper transfer prices, reallocate income, impose a hidden-distribution treatment on amounts repatriated to the non-resident parent/foundation, and apply penalties of up to PAB 10,000 plus interest and late-payment surcharges for failure to maintain and file TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the Foundation Council who knowingly approve artificial related-party margins may be jointly and severally liable for the resulting tax deficiency and penalties, and may face personal attachment and travel limitations in serious non-compliance cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Dividend and Cross-Border Withholding Tax Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Passing economic profits from the Panamanian operating IVD company to non-resident shareholders through untaxed distributions, artificially low-priced service payments, or royalty payments to an offshore IP shell without withholding at the statutory 5%, 10%, or 12.5% rates, or without valid treaty certificates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent is personally deemed the taxpayer for the unwithheld amounts, with liability for the full tax, a 10% surcharge, monthly interest, and penalties. Criminal sanctions may apply if the non-withholding was carried out as part of a scheme to deceive the DGI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who direct the payment of dividends or royalties without applying the required withholding may be civilly liable for the unpaid tax and penalties; repeated violations can support criminal prosecution and the restriction of travel pending payment of the tax debt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Private Interest Foundation to obscure the natural person behind the IVD manufacturer, processing Swift LC or TT wire payments without proper customer due diligence or distributor KYC, transacting with sanctioned or high-risk counterparties, or structuring deposits to avoid scrutiny under Panama's AML framework.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 23 of 2015, regulated service providers and the foundation council can be fined severely for AML deficiencies; criminal money-laundering prosecution can lead to asset forfeiture and imprisonment. The AML risk tier for this cross-border medical device commercial model is Medium-Risk Enhanced, requiring CDD, wire monitoring, and beneficial ownership records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, Foundation Council members, and compliance officers can be personally prosecuted, with penalties including imprisonment, civil asset confiscation, travel bans, and prohibition from serving as directors of any Panamanian juridical entity.
